papers_read.title_as_printed: A prediction nomogram for mild cognitive impairment in type 2 diabetes mellitus based on the Chinese visceral adiposity index (Zhou et al., Scientific Reports 2025;15:32393)
Explainable machine learning models for identifying mild cognitive impairment in older patients with chronic pain (Zhang et al., BMC Nursing 2025;24:72)

what_each_reports.P-339: Logistic-regression nomogram (age, gender, education, CVAI) for MoCA-defined MCI (MoCA < 26) in 337 hospitalised T2DM patients aged 40-75 at one Nanjing hospital: AUC 0.765 (95% CI 0.705-0.826) in the training cohort (n = 236) and 0.690 (95% CI 0.588-0.792) in the random 30% validation cohort (n = 101); optimism-corrected C-index 0.747.
what_each_reports.P-307: XGBoost on seven variables (age, education, pain duration, number of pain sites, VAS pain level, GDS-15 depression, PSQI sleep) for MCI (Petersen/IWG criteria, MoCA < 26 plus complaint, ADL and neurologist confirmation) in 612 chronic-pain patients aged >= 60 at one Nanchang pain department: AUC 0.925 (95% CI 0.863-0.995) on the 30% test set after SMOTETomek balancing.

quantity_a: ROC-AUC of a four-variable demographic + visceral-adiposity nomogram for cross-sectional MoCA-defined MCI vs normal cognition in hospitalised Chinese T2DM patients aged 40-75 (training cohort 0.765; held-out 0.690).
quantity_b: ROC-AUC of an XGBoost model on pain, depression, sleep and demographic variables for clinically diagnosed MCI vs non-MCI in Chinese outpatients/inpatients aged >= 60 with chronic pain (held-out test set).
incompatible_if_same: Only superficially: the training-cohort interval of P-339 (0.705-0.826) does not overlap P-307's (0.863-0.995), but P-339's own held-out figure is 0.690 and neither study evaluates the other's model or population, so no ordering claimed by one is refuted by the other; the gap is between two different models in two different populations.

gates.task: match in the broad sense (both cross-sectional MCI vs non-MCI detection, T1), although the registry codes P-339 as T4; the record's 'T1' for P-339 is not what the registry holds.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: two separate single-centre hospital cohorts (Affiliated Zhongda Hospital, Nanjing, T2DM inpatients; 1st Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University, chronic-pain patients). No waiver on record.
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal random split (V2), no external cohort.
gates.modality_family: match in family (clinical/tabular) but the predictor sets are disjoint apart from age and education (CVAI and sex vs pain intensity, pain sites, pain duration, depression, sleep). The record's 'P-307=retinal' is wrong; P-307 uses no imaging.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric type (ROC-AUC) but different populations behind the shared 'MCI' label (T2DM inpatients 40-75 vs chronic-pain patients >= 60), different MCI definitions (MoCA < 26 alone vs Petersen/IWG criteria with neurologist confirmation), and P-339's quoted 0.765 is an apparent training-cohort AUC while P-307's 0.925 is a held-out test AUC.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither study reaches 0.97 (P-307's 0.925 is the highest); the candidate is a performance comparison but the automatic test is not tripped.
independence: Independent: different authors, institutions and cohorts.
grounds: The two AUCs describe different populations behind the shared MCI label: hospitalised T2DM patients aged 40-75 in P-339 against chronic-pain patients aged 60 or over in P-307.
The predictor sets are different (demographics plus visceral adiposity index vs pain, depression and sleep scales), so the AUCs measure different models, not one quantity estimated twice.
The dataset-family gate fails (two unrelated single-centre cohorts) and no waiver is recorded.
P-339's quoted 0.765 is the training-cohort AUC; its held-out AUC is 0.690, which the record omits.
Neither paper evaluates or makes a claim about the other's population or model, so no ordering claimed by one is contradicted by the other.

evidence_quotes.quote: A total of 337 hospitalized patients with T2DM were included and randomly assigned to a training cohort (70%, n = 236) and a validation cohort (30%, n = 101).
MoCA score ≥ 26 is considered normal (NC group) and MoCA score <26 is considered MCI(MCI group)
identified four robust predictors in the training cohort: age, gender, education, and CVAI.
with AUC values of 0.765 (95% CI: 0.705–0.826) in the training cohort and 0.690 (95% CI 0.588–0.792) in the validation cohort (Fig. 4C, D).
A total of 612 older patients with chronic pain were recruited between October 2023 and July 2024.
the final selected variables were: age, education level, pain duration, number of pain sites, pain level, depression, sleep quality
the XGBoost model performed best, achieving an accuracy of 0.883 and an AUC of 0.925 (95% CI 0.863–0.995).

record_defects: resolution_note states 'Modality mismatch: P-339=clinical_survey vs P-307=retinal'; P-307 uses questionnaire and clinical variables only, no retinal data.
dataset_equal is 'Yes'; the two studies use unrelated single-hospital cohorts in different cities and populations.
claim_a gives P-339 AUC 0.765 without saying it is the training-cohort figure; the held-out validation AUC is 0.690.
claim_a labels P-339 as T1 while the registry row codes it T4.
The bridging-evidence list (P-360, P-5, P-6, P-19, P-38, ...) names no condition separating the two results; it is a list of unrelated performance figures.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A study applying one of the two models to the other's population (or both models to one cohort) with the same MCI definition; absent that, the two AUCs are not estimates of the same quantity.
